tested.name: Recent seasons weighted 35% / 15% (instead of 60% / 30%)
tested.result: QB yards gain 0.0184 vs 0.0169, anytime TD 0.0048 vs 0.0046, team FGs o1.5 -0.0069 vs -0.0091 (log loss vs baseline, 3 seasons)

tested.name: Team touchdown / turnover rates shrunk with 300 pseudo-drives (instead of 120)
tested.result: halves, field goals and QB yards all slightly better; the model-alone game lines slightly worse (they are not used)

tested.name: Field-goal tries shrunk with 600 pseudo-drives, kicker with 150 attempts
tested.result: team FGs o1.5 -0.0030 vs -0.0043; heavier shrinkage (2000) and no roof effect did not help further

tested.name: Market anchor moves field-goal tries 30% as much as touchdowns
tested.result: team FGs o1.5 turned from -0.0030 to +0.0029, o0.5 from -0.0045 to +0.0020 (higher-scoring games produce touchdowns, not more field goals); 0% was worse than 30%

tested.name: Team half shapes (separate first- and second-half rates)
tested.result: 1st half +0.0006 without it, 2nd half and field goals worse without it: mixed, kept on

tested.name: Keep part of the model's disagreement with the closing spread / total
tested.result: regression weight -0.17 ± 0.11 (spread) and 0.03 ± 0.14 (total): no information beyond the line

tested.name: Key-number correction of the margin distribution (more 3s and 7s)
tested.result: trained on 2023-24 and tested on 2025: cover / push / miss log loss 0.71086 vs 0.71092, below the threshold

tested.name: Players' own games weighted with a 6-game half-life (instead of 12)
tested.result: anytime TD gain 0.0069 vs 0.0049 (log loss vs each player's own rate, 14,788 player-games)

tested.name: Touchdown shares scaled by the recent change in snap share (last two games vs his average, pulled halfway to 1)
tested.result: anytime TD gain 0.0071 vs 0.0049 alone, 0.0082 together with the 6-game half-life; full weight (not halfway) 0.0080

tested.name: Receiving-yards props from usage shares x simulated passing yards (noise sd = k sqrt(expected))
tested.result: 6,902 player-games 2023-25, over/under at each player's trailing-average line: log-loss gain 0.0380 +/- 0.0042 vs the trailing average; median error 22.8 yds vs 24.3

tested.name: Rushing-yards props from carry share x simulated rushes x player YPC
tested.result: 3,231 player-games: gain 0.0218 +/- 0.0074 vs the trailing average; median error 22.8 yds vs 24.1

tested.name: Receptions props from reception share x simulated completions
tested.result: 7,182 player-games: gain 0.0323 +/- 0.0046 vs the trailing average; median error 1.63 vs 1.71

tested.name: Player candidates chosen from pregame rosters and injury reports (look-ahead removed)
tested.result: the test used to pick touchdown and yardage candidates from who touched the ball in the game; it now uses that week's active roster minus Out / Doubtful, exactly as the live page does, and settles only players who took the field (a scratch is a void bet). Anytime TD gain 0.0218 +/- 0.0015 over 17,710 player-games; yardage props unchanged; listed candidates score 96.5% of team touchdowns

tested.name: All markets read from one market-reweighted distribution (halves, field goals, passing, players share the moneyline / spread weights)
tested.result: 1st half 0.0003 vs -0.0009, 2nd half 0.0010 vs 0.0004, QB TDs over 1.5 0.0111 vs 0.0087 (now beats baseline), QB yards and yardage props unchanged; the cards and the parlay slip now price from the same joint distribution

tested.name: Overtime rules (2025: both teams possess after a first-drive touchdown, then next score wins, defensive scores end it, clock expiry ties)
tested.result: unit-tested rule by rule; simulated overtime rate 4.5% vs 5.3% actual (2023-25), simulated ties 0.3% vs 0.1%

tested.name: Lighter shrinkage on quarterback volume and efficiency (dropbacks 100 -> 30 or 15 pseudo-drives, yards per dropback 250 -> 120 or 60, recent seasons 20% / 5%)
tested.result: Walk-forward on 2025 weeks 2-18 and 2026 weeks 2-5 (622 QB games): the projections stop being too compressed (actual-vs-projected slope 1.30 -> 1.07 / 0.97) but get less accurate (mean absolute error 54.6 -> 54.7 / 55.0 yds, log loss 0.670 -> 0.672 / 0.674). In 2026 the model still under-projects the top third of passers by about 20 yds under every setting. Not adopted: the projection cannot be fixed by retuning, so passing props are now priced from the market and the model may only nudge them (nfl/value.py).

pros: Five targets in four games; never more than two in a game; one game with zero

The sim and the market both lean the same way; the desk's mean of 1.0 reception needs two catches to lose
risks: Four-game sample; a single screen-heavy drive or a checkdown game produces two receptions
Rice out and Thornton on IR free targets that could drift to backs; Reid uses backs in the passing game

desk.verdict: Measured volume and YPC put the median near 72-75 yards against DraftKings' 90.5; under at 1.88 is a 59% play, with Warren's game-time decision and a blowout script as the named risks. Confirm Warren's status when inactives post at 11:30 ET.
pros: Taylor has not reached 90 in any 2026 game and is at 3.9 YPC on 101 carries
TEN's run defense is mid-pack by EPA and allowed 3.54 YPC through week 5
The line moved up to 90.5 and the spread shortened to -6.5, both small helps to the under; IND's drives stall into field goals (Shrader 16/16)
risks: Tyler Warren is a game-time decision (groin): if he is inactive, the run share rises and the mean moves to about 79 (P(under) 0.61)
Blowout script: a two-score IND lead means 25+ carries and 90.5 is reachable at 3.6 YPC
Taylor's last three games against Tennessee produced 218, 102 and 153 yards; one long run skews the right tail beyond a 0.5 x mean SD
TEN's 3.54 YPC allowed is from the earlier run's PFR fetch, not re-verified today
inputs: Feed 2026-10-18T12:15Z: DraftKings Taylor rushing yards 90.5, over 1.90 / under 1.88 (yesterday's 89.5 is gone; re-keyed to the board's 90.5 entry)

Taylor 2026: 101 carries, 398 yds, 3.9 YPC; carries 19/24/23/20/15 (20.5 per game last four); no 2026 game at 90+ rushing yards (Football Nation Oct 16; payload anytime block); full practice all week (Colts on SI Oct 16)
Carry share 74% of IND rushes this season (payload); IND about 27 rushes a game, 64 plays at a 57% neutral pass rate
TEN run defense: rank 15 by rush EPA allowed, -0.069 EPA per rush (payload rank_def/adv); 3.54 YPC allowed per the earlier run's PFR fetch (not re-fetched today)
Named reason for sitting above the market: Taylor's own 3.9 YPC against a defense allowing 3.54; the simulation's mean is 75.4 and median 73.4 (payload props_sim)
Script: DraftKings IND -6.5 (opened -7), total 44.5, sim margin +3.4; Tyler Warren (TE, 21% target share) is a game-time decision: if he sits, Indianapolis leans more on the run
arithmetic: Carries: 27 team rushes x 0.74 = 20; favourite script +1 = 21
YPC: own 3.9 x (TEN 3.54 allowed / league 4.3) = 3.2; blend 2/3 adjusted + 1/3 own = 3.44
Mean = 21 x 3.44 = 72 yds (sim mean 75.4, median 73.4); SD = 0.5 x 72 = 36
P(under 90.5) = Phi((90.5 - 72) / 36) = Phi(0.51) = 0.69 raw; sim quantiles give about 0.65 (site p_model 0.66); Warren-out case 23 carries, mean 79, P(under) = 0.61

Market no-vig under at 1.88 / 1.90 = 0.50; sim 0.66; raw desk 0.69 is 19 points above the market (re-check trigger): the market has priced his form and the under moved a yard in our favour without news, so the desk sits at 0.59, not 0.69

desk.verdict: Take Williams under 68.5 rushing yards at DraftKings 1.90: 14.8 carries at under 4.0 per carry puts his mean near 59 against a number set at 68.5. The risk is GB's thin interior and a DAL lead; confidence is moderate because the run-defense leg is an estimate.
pros: Volume is steady but modest (12 to 19 carries) and efficiency is poor (3.7 YPC), so 68.5 needs a top-quartile game
DAL is the league's most pass-heavy offense by PROE and is a small underdog; a trailing or neutral script keeps the carries near 13-15
Pinnacle shades the under at the same number; the simulation (0.67) agrees
risks: GB's interior is depleted (Hargrave out for the season, Ford out, Riley doubtful, Campbell questionable): a soft run front raises YPC, and Williams had 19-carry games against BAL and HOU
If DAL leads late, carries rise past 18 and the under is in danger
GB's YPC allowed was not measured today; the evidence is partial
inputs: Williams carries this season 12, 12, 19, 19, 12 = 14.8 per game (payload recent); 59% carry share; snaps 76-85%
Yards per carry 3.7 this season (previous desk run, StatSniper game logs, Oct 17); multi-season blend in the payload 4.16; desk uses 3.87 (two-thirds this season, one-third prior)
GB run defense: rush EPA allowed -0.017 (rank 20), run-defense yds per carry allowed not measured today (estimate: x1.03 vs league), so one leg is an estimate

Game script: DAL +1.5 road underdog, 64% neutral pass rate with the league's highest PROE (+1.4%); GB's defense is light inside (Hargrave, Ford out, Riley doubtful, Campbell questionable), which is the main way the over hits
DraftKings 68.5 (-114/-110) in the 12:15Z feed; Pinnacle 68.5 with the under shaded to 1.82 (implied 0.55); consensus 67.5
Simulation: rush yds mean 55.8, 75th percentile 77.1, P(under 68.5) 0.67; site p 0.53
Availability: Williams carries no designation; DAL on 10 days' rest after the Thursday loss to TB
arithmetic: Carries = 14.8 (season average, 59% share of about 25 team rushes)
YPC = 3.87 x 1.03 (GB run D slightly below average by EPA; estimate) = 3.98

Market no-vig at DraftKings 1.88/1.90: under 0.497; Pinnacle's shaded under implies 0.55; simulation 0.67; desk 0.62 is 12 points above DraftKings' no-vig, past the trigger. Re-checked: the reason is that the line (68.5) is 10 yds above his carries x YPC this season (55); the market prices GB's thin interior and a possible DAL lead; confidence lowered to 40 because the YPC-allowed leg is an estimate

desk.verdict: Take Kraft under 52.5 receiving yards at DraftKings 1.88 (-114): the number sits 10 yards above his season mean and 3 above the sharp market, and the skewed distribution puts his median near 42. Pass if DraftKings is 47.5 or lower by kickoff.
pros: Line is 10 yards above Kraft's season mean and 3 above the rest of the market; his median outcome this season is about 42
GB's passing volume flows to Watson and Golden against the league's worst pass defense; the over needs Kraft to steal targets or break a long catch-and-run
Simulation (0.74) and both desk distributions (0.64 to 0.73) agree on the side; the line moved 2 yds in the under's favour since yesterday
risks: One explosive play beats the under: Kraft had a 46-yard catch in week 5 and two 60+ games in five; DAL allows an 89.7% catch rate to TEs and plays base against 12 personnel, which GB used 27-30% the last two weeks
If Watson or Golden leaves the game, Kraft's target share jumps; a shootout (total 53.5) adds attempts
Price is the 12:15Z feed; if DraftKings drops back to 49.5 or lower before kickoff the edge thins (desk 0.57 at 49.5)
inputs: Kraft 2026: 29 targets, 20 catches, 212 yds in 5 games = 5.8 targets and 42.4 yds per game, 7.3 yds per target; game log 65, 15, 26, 42, 64 (3 of 5 under 52.5)
Target share 29/185 GB attempts = 15.7% (payload tgt_share 16.5% incl. prior); recent targets 6, 3, 8, 7, 5; snaps 76-92%
GB 37 attempts per game (Love 185 attempts in 5 games); desk uses 36 against a DAL defense that invites passing (neutral pass 61%, PROE -0.5%)

DAL allows 8.3 yds per target to TEs vs about 7.5 league (x1.11), blended half-weight with Kraft's own 7.3 = 7.7 yds per target; DAL pass defense last in EPA (+0.376) and success rate, which feeds Watson and Golden (48% of GB targets, 92% of air yards)
DraftKings moved 50.5 (Sat) to 52.5 (feed 12:15Z, -110/-114); consensus and Pinnacle 49.5: DraftKings is 3 yds above the market
Simulation: Kraft rec yds mean 36.5, 75th percentile 53.2, P(under 52.5) 0.74; site p 0.53
Availability: Kraft, Watson and Golden carry no designation; Skyy Moore (WR) out, Savion Williams (WR) questionable off IR: no target-share change for Kraft (Packers On SI Oct 16)
Weather: clear, 56 F, SSW 11-12 mph, gusts possible near 20, no rain: no effect on short targets
arithmetic: Targets = 36 attempts x 0.157 = 5.65
Mean = 5.65 x 7.7 yds per target = 43.5 yds
SD = 0.6 x 43.5 = 26 (right-skewed)
Lognormal with the same mean and SD: sigma 0.555, mu 3.619, P(under 52.5) = Phi((3.961 - 3.619) / 0.555) = Phi(0.62) = 0.73
Empirical: 3 of 5 games under 52.5; season mean 42.4. Desk p = 0.61 (normal figure, trimmed for the two 60+ games)

Market no-vig at DraftKings 1.90/1.88: under 0.503; simulation 0.74; desk 0.61 sits 10.7 points above the market, past the 8-point trigger. Re-checked: the reason is DraftKings' number (52.5) sitting 3 yds above Pinnacle and the consensus (49.5) with Kraft's season median near 42; at 49.5 the desk would be 0.57

desk.verdict: Under 52.5 at 1.98: the measured scoring bases are 42-46 and the market's 52.5 was built on quarterback news; take the under, sized for a B grade with the QB adjustment named as the open estimate.
pros: Both offenses are slow and run-leaning (ATL PROE -11.4%, 47% neutral pass; CHI 53%) and the two defenses rank top-six (ATL) and top-two on third down (CHI)
Every measured base is under 46; the market number is built on two quarterback returns, one of them a first game back from a torn hamstring
Dome removes weather variance but adds only about a point
risks: Caleb Williams in full health lifts Chicago's ceiling (59 points at CAR in week 1); a Bagent-type start is already out of the number
Both secondaries are short: ATL without C.J. Henderson and A.J. Terrell, CHI with Stevenson and Gordon Questionable, which can push passing efficiency up
The desk is 12 points from the market; the QB adjustment is an estimate and the sim's raw figure may undershoot the 2026 offenses
Chicago's run defense (26th EPA/rush, 4 front-seven players out) can give Bijan Robinson long drives that end in touchdowns
inputs: DraftKings total 52.5 (over 1.85 / under 1.98) in the 12:15Z feed; DK opened 50.5, was 47.5 on Oct 13 before the Williams/Penix news, 52.5 since Friday: the whole move came with quarterback news, not scoring
Points per drive (payload, 56-game blend): ATL offense 1.935, CHI defense allows 2.005; CHI offense 2.074, ATL defense allows 2.023
Pace: ATL 169.7 s per offensive drive (32.9 s/play, PROE -11.4%, neutral pass rate 47%), CHI 178.7 s per drive (30.7 s/play): about 10.5 drives each
2026 scoring: ATL 23.8 for / 24.4 against per game (5 games), CHI 23.8 for / 19.2 against; cross-match average 45.6
Defenses: ATL 4th in success rate and explosive rate allowed, 6th red-zone TD allowed; CHI 2nd on third down, 7th sack rate (but 26th EPA/rush, 24th explosive)
Simulation raw total 42.5 (with Williams at QB); it is anchored to the market at 52.4 for the site's props
Caleb Williams expected to start (SI 09:55Z today citing Schefter/Rapoport/Garafolo; officially Questionable, hamstring, full practice all week); Penix no limitations (AJC 10/16)
Dome, turf, both teams on 7 days' rest
arithmetic: Drives: 3600 s / 174 s per drive = 20.7 drives, 10.4 each (call it 10.5)

Adjustments to the higher base (45.6): dome +1.0 (payload dome factor), Williams for Bagent +2.5 (estimate: Williams 220 yds/1.4 TD per game 2025 vs Bagent 87 yds, 2 INT last week), Penix fully fit +0.5 = desk mean 49.5; shaded to 49.0 for the slow pace of both offenses

Market: no-vig under 0.483 (1/1.98 = 0.505, 1/1.85 = 0.541); simulation (anchored) 0.516; desk 0.60: 12 points above the market, a re-check trigger. Reason named: the 5-point rise from 47.5 came entirely on QB news while every measured scoring base (42 by drives, 45.6 by season scoring) sits 7-10 points under the number; the QB adjustments are estimates, so confidence is lowered to 50 and evidence is partial

desk.verdict: A 2-3 target tight end against a 2.5 line: under 2.5 receptions at 1.62 is about 65% on the measured target trend; the catch-rate leg is estimated, so this is a B with a thin price margin.
pros: Helm's targets have fallen to 2, 4, 2, 1 as Tate and Robinson absorb 52% of the targets; he has one game with 3+ catches' worth of targets in the last four
Spears' return adds a check-down option (9 targets last week), and Tennessee's -8% PROE caps pass volume
Three receptions needs three targets converted on a 2-3 target diet
risks: Trailing script: TEN threw 40 dropbacks last week; a 40+ dropback game adds a target or two
Catch rate is an estimate, not a measured 2026 figure; a 3-for-3 game on short throws beats the number
If Spears is a late scratch, Ward's check-downs flow to the tight ends
The 1.62 price leaves a 3-point margin over break-even; a thin edge at a short price

desk.verdict: Drive-level arithmetic puts this game at 37.5-38 with Huntley starting and both offenses slow; the under at 39.5 is a modest edge at 1.93 and still playable down to 38.5.
pros: Both offenses are slow and run-first, and the Ravens' plan with Huntley (35 runs vs 32 attempts at ATL, 3.8 air yards per attempt) burns clock: fewer drives than a normal game
Cleveland's offense is bottom-five by success rate and third down and gives up the league's highest sack rate, against a BAL pass defense that is league average and a BAL run defense ranked 11th
The line already fell from 42.5 to 39.5 on the Jackson news and the desk's drive arithmetic still sits two points below it
risks: Huntley's last three starts averaged 33.7 team points (Newsweek), and the simulation's own backup-QB cut (calibrated BAL 21.4) is smaller than some of those games suggest; if BAL scores 27 the under needs CLE held to 12
Cleveland is down three interior DTs (Hall Jr., Davis, Graham): Henry's explosive runs can shorten BAL drives into quick touchdowns rather than clock-eating ones
Turnovers from a rookie-center BAL line against the NFL's 5th-ranked sack-rate defense, or short fields from Watson's 19 sacks, add scores on either side; a wind of 9 mph gives the under no help
inputs: Lamar Jackson OUT (official report; Newsweek Oct 16, News5 Oct 16); Tyler Huntley starts: 3.8 intended air yards per attempt, BAL ran 35 times vs 32 attempts in his start at ATL; BAL pass rate over expected -9.1% on the season
Pace: BAL 168 seconds per drive, CLE 150 (payload offense.secs_per_drive), about 22.6 drives in the game, 10.8 each after end-of-half possessions
Points per drive: BAL offense 2.455 vs CLE defense 1.826 allowed; CLE offense 1.387 vs BAL defense 2.019 allowed (payload research, league baseline 2.0)
CLE offense 28th in success rate, 31st on third down (29.5%), 32nd in sack rate allowed (Watson sacked 19 times in 5 games); CLE scored 10/23/21/27/12 (18.6 per game)
CLE pass defense 6th by EPA and 5th in sack rate vs a BAL line with rookie C Ioane and both guards questionable; BAL run defense 11th by EPA, 6th in success rate
Weather: 59.5F, wind 9 mph gusting 14, 0% rain (payload Open-Meteo this morning): no adjustment either way
Simulation: calibrated total mean 39.53, fair line 38.5, P(under 39.5) 0.517; market total opened 42.5 and sits at 39.5 (DraftKings and Pinnacle)
arithmetic: Drives: 3600 s / 159 s average per drive = 22.6, about 10.8 per team
BAL: 2.455 x (1.826 / 2.0) = 2.24 pts/drive x 10.8 = 24.2 with Jackson; backup-QB cut -4.5 (simulation's calibrated away points 21.4; Huntley 23 regulation points at ATL) = 20.0 (estimate leg)
CLE: 1.387 x (2.019 / 2.0) = 1.40 pts/drive x 10.8 = 15.1 + home field 1.5 = 16.6; blended one-to-one with 18.6 scored per game = 17.5
Desk total = 20.0 + 17.5 = 37.5 (yesterday 38); SD 13.5; P(under 39.5) = Phi((39.5 - 37.5) / 13.5) = Phi(0.15) = 0.56, rounded down to 0.55 for the estimate leg
Market no-vig at over 1.89 / under 1.93: under 0.518 / (0.529 + 0.518) = 0.495; simulation 0.517; desk 0.55 is +5.5 points on the market, +3.3 on the simulation

desk.verdict: At 70.5 the desk has Hubbard about 9 yards clear on 17 to 18 carries with Dillon out; play the over at 70.5 (1.87) or lower, pass at 74.5 or higher, and confirm Etienne's role at inactives.

5.0 YPC this season against a PHI front that is 24th in rush EPA allowed
CAR is the favourite against a weakened PHI offense (McKee confirmed, no Barkley, Dickerson out): the script that feeds carries
DraftKings' line is a yard lower than yesterday (70.5) at the same price
risks: Etienne is expected to be active and could take 6 to 8 touches, which drops Hubbard toward 15 carries and a 68-yard mean
PHI's 4.0 YPC allowed is below league average; at 4.0 YPC the mean is 71 and the edge is gone
A CAR deficit (Week 1: 10 carries) or a pass-heavy script (PROE +4.8%) caps volume
Hubbard's 5.0 YPC is a 61-carry sample; the simulation's 26% says the market is already generous

desk.verdict: Walker's 21-22 carries at even a shaded 4.7 YPC clear 90.5 more often than not against a run-first visitor that should trail. Play to 90.5 at 1.85 or better; pass at 95.5.
pros: Three of four games over 90.5 on a workload that has not dipped below 18 carries; the league's best rushing offence by EPA
Script favours the run: 7.5-point favourite, slow pace on both sides, LAC a run-first 0-5 team that keeps the clock moving
Yesterday's desk had the side at 0.55 on 91.5 but no DraftKings price; the feed now prices it a point lower
risks: LAC's run defence ranks 8th by EPA and 7th by success rate; 70 yards at MIA shows the floor on 18 carries
6.17 YPC over four games is not sustainable; the desk's 4.7 is a judgement with the LAC YPC-allowed figure unmeasured
A LAC lead or a tight game shifts KC to Mahomes; the sim's 71-yard mean is the other view
Questionable DL Tomlinson and Caldwell and LB Henley: if they play, the interior is closer to full strength

desk.summary: Sunday-morning final pass on the twelve Sunday games still to kick off plus Monday night, after Saturday's roster moves and the morning's feed: Lamar Jackson, Baker Mayfield and Jalen Hurts out (Huntley, Daniels, McKee start), Caleb Williams and A.J. Brown expected to play, Tyler Warren a game-time call. DraftKings moved several prop lines overnight without news, so most of yesterday's picks were re-keyed to today's feed lines; four supported props (Cook, Allen, Likely, Metcalf) were set aside only because their sections were full, and Houston at Jacksonville kicked off before this pass and keeps its published picks.

notes: Wembley Stadium (neutral site, outdoors, grass), kickoff 14:30 BST. Saturday roster news (Oct 17): HOU activated LB Henry To'oTo'o and CB Ja'Marcus Ingram to the 53 and elevated RB Jawhar Jordan and CB Bryce Hall (heavy.com, 14:50 ET); JAX signed S Kaevon Merriweather to the 53 and elevated LS Jacob Bobenmoyer (replaces Matiscik, Out) and CB Jabbar Muhammad (Yahoo, 20:12 UTC). The CB elevation hints that Q CB Jaylon Jones (hamstring, LP all week) is in doubt; no Saturday source said either way.

HOU is without RB1 David Montgomery, S/nickel Jalen Pitre and WR Tank Dell (all Out, final report Oct 16). Woody Marks starts at RB (15 carries, 4 catches, 85% snaps in Week 5 after Montgomery left; Ogunbowale and the elevated Jordan behind him). Marvin Harrison Jr. (acquired Oct 11) is set to debut in a limited package per the earlier run's Oct 14 AP report; Nico Collins is healthy (10, 8, 7 targets in his three games). JAX is without LT Anton Harrison (IR Oct 13; Walker Little starts) and CB Montaric Brown (Out).

Matchup: JAX defense ranks 1st in rush EPA and 7th in pass EPA with 14.0 points allowed per game (70 in 5); HOU defense ranks 3rd in sack rate (9.0%, 18 sacks) and 7th in rush EPA, 19th in pass EPA, and loses its tight-end/slot defender Pitre. JAX sack rate allowed 6.3% with a first-time LT against that rush.

Usage: Stroud 36 dropbacks per game this season (41, 57, 30, 31, 36), 274/353/167/347/261 yards; Lawrence 30.6 dropbacks (24, 31, 29, 28, 41), 245/189/182/227/331. Strange targets 3, 2, 5, 8, 8 (snaps 77-87%); Washington 6, 12, 5, 3, 9 targets; Tuten 15, 13, 15, 17, 22 carries (snap share 48% to 68%). Schultz 8, 14, 3, 2, 4 targets with Collins back.

Game script: DraftKings JAX -2.5 (-115 / -105), total 42.5 (O -112 / U -108), ML HOU +124 / JAX -148, unchanged from the feed (statsniper book table, Oct 17). Both offenses are slow (JAX 175 s per drive, HOU 165) for about 10.6 drives each; neutral pass rates 59% and PROE -3.4% / -3.3% for both. Earlier run found DK opened -3 / 43.5 (SI, Oct 12): one point toward HOU and one off the total without an injury trigger.

Totals context from the payload: JAX games 44, 33, 41, 39, 36 (1-4 to the over); HOU games 67, 26, 36, 64, 29. Points-per-drive pairing (JAX 2.21 vs HOU 1.79 allowed; HOU 1.93 vs JAX 1.76 allowed) gives 40.7 before weather; the simulation says 42.8 to 45.2.

Situational: both teams on 7 days rest. JAX played PHI at Tottenham last week and stayed in London (per the earlier run, not re-verified today); HOU travelled across the Atlantic this week. Cam Little 9/11 with a 57-yard winner last week; Fairbairn 11/12. No coordinator changes found.

Not verified today: DraftKings player-prop prices (Scores and Odds, legionreport blocked; statsniper shows no props posted). The Strange receptions price is the earlier run's 17:17Z reading of the DK column and is listed as unverified. No DK line found for Woody Marks or Tuten rushing yards, Collins receiving yards, or Washington over 4.5 receptions.

notes: Availability (final pass, 2026-10-18T13:50Z): no Saturday or Sunday change to the Friday reports was found. The Questionable players a bettor must confirm when inactives post at 18:35Z: LA CB Trent McDuffie (groin, pulled at the end of Thursday practice, DNP Friday; McVay called sitting him Friday 'precautionary', no expected-to-play note), LA S Kam Curl (ankle, DNP Friday; McVay: 'we feel good about him'), ARI S Budda Baker (rest/groin, DNP Friday after a full Thursday), ARI LB Zaven Collins (hip, DNP Friday), ARI S Kitan Crawford (ankle, on IR with the 21-day window opened 10-14; must have been activated Saturday to play, no activation found) and P Blake Gillikin (back). Out: ARI RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee), S Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion). TE Davis Allen (foot) has no designation and is 'trending in the right direction'; Higbee and Byron Young were Friday rest days only.

Quarterbacks: Jacoby Brissett starts for Arizona (feed: all sources agree, no status; the only other Cardinals QB on the Friday report is Carson Beck, back, Limited Friday, no designation; Kyler Murray is not on the report). Matthew Stafford starts for the Rams with David Quessenberry at left tackle (Alaric Jackson suspended). No Sunday-dated page on either quarterback was found within the search budget; searches for Arizona's Saturday roster moves returned only 2024-2025 pages.

Lines (DraftKings feed 2026-10-18T12:15Z): LA -12.5 (1.89 / ARI +12.5 1.93), total 51.5 (over 1.87 / under 1.95), ML LA 1.12 / ARI 6.5. Spread unchanged from the feed opener (-12.5) with Pinnacle a point higher at -13.5; total unchanged at 51.5 in the feed (VegasInsider's early opener was 47.5 per yesterday's run); moneyline has tightened from 7.0/1.11 to 6.5/1.12. Props have moved toward the unders since Thursday without injury news: Stafford 283.5 to 279.5 (DK 1.89/1.89; Pinnacle 279.5 with the over shaded to 1.78), Brissett 243.5 to 236.5.

Stafford form and usage: 155, 327, 390, 317, 383 passing yards on 25, 31, 57, 52, 56 dropbacks; 7.23 yards per dropback over the last four, 7.11 on the season; four straight 300-yard games. Rams neutral pass rate 64.6%, PROE +3.8%, 29.3 seconds per play; 52 to 57 dropbacks in three straight games including a 24-20 win at PHI. January meeting as a 14.5-point favourite: 40 dropbacks, 259 yards.

Matchup: Arizona's defense is 31st by pass EPA allowed (+0.349 per dropback), 7.07 yards per dropback allowed (1.04x league), 31st in explosive plays allowed, 83% red-zone TD allowed (31st); its run defense is 4th by EPA (-0.158), which caps Kyren Williams (67.5 line, sim mean 67.4). The Rams' defense is 5th by pass EPA (-0.105) and 5th on third down (32%). Arizona's offense is 32nd in explosive-play rate; Brissett 4.87 yards per dropback over his last four (95/280/166/292 on 30/53/37/51). McDuffie's absence would move Watson, Wallace and Forbes up against Wilson and McBride; cornerback shadow assignments unmeasured.

Game script: 12.5-point favourite in a 51.5 total (simulation 32-19). A Rams lead is the only thing that trims Stafford's and Nacua's volume, so both selections are weighted 30% early-blowout / 45% normal / 25% competitive in the arithmetic; Arizona trailing lifts Brissett's dropbacks (53 and 51 in its two shootout losses), which is why the Brissett under 236.5 is a coin flip and not taken.

Nacua usage: 9, 12 and 24 targets in his three 2026 games (he missed weeks 2 and 3), 32.3% target share, snap share 0.70 / 0.90 / 0.85; no 2026 catch rate is in the payload, so the receptions arithmetic uses an estimated 0.72 and the grade is C.

Situational and stadium: Rams on six days after Monday night, Cardinals on seven; no time-zone change; SoFi fixed roof, turf, no weather. Rams kicker is Blake Grupe (payload kicker block stale); special teams remain the Rams' weak unit.

declined.label: Rachaad White rush yds (either side of 47.5)
declined.why: Croskey-Merritt is out and the White/Ekeler/McNichols split is unmeasured (White 7 to 8 carries a game so far); the line already prices the vacated carries; unmeasured evidence.

declined.label: Austin Ekeler under 19.5 rush yds
declined.why: Simulation's 0.72 does not know Croskey-Merritt is out; Ekeler's carries rise by an unmeasured amount; declined.

declined.label: Christian McCaffrey rush yds (either side of 61.5)
declined.why: 13.7 carries the last three games x 4.3 = 59, but a favourite's script and Kaelon Black's possible absence (personal matter) add carries; mean 59 to 64 brackets the line.

declined.label: Christian McCaffrey rec yds under 39.5 and recs under 4.5
declined.why: With Deebo and Evans out his targets rise above the simulation's 4.6; mean about 38 to 42 yards and 4.5 receptions, no edge.

declined.label: Jayden Daniels under 38.5 rush yds
declined.why: Carries 5, 7, 8 this season at 6.7 a carry give 33 to 54; this-season rushing yards per game unmeasured; SD 0.5 x mean; coin flip.

declined.label: Kaelon Black under 24.5 rush yds
declined.why: Missed practice for a personal matter; availability unknown and 6 carries a game is too thin.

declined.label: Brock Purdy under 19.5 rush yds
declined.why: Carries 5, 3, 1, 8, 3 this season; mean 18 with SD 9, P(under) about 0.56 at 1.86 (break-even 0.538); thin evidence, left off to keep the game at two stronger selections.

declined.label: Jayden Daniels under 1.5 pass TDs
declined.why: Passing-touchdown markets are off in the owner's spec.

excluded.label: Brenton Strange over 3.5 receptions
excluded.why: price never confirmed on DraftKings (the spec takes DraftKings' posted lines only)

sections.label: QB props
sections.note: passing yards only; no over/under TD passes

best.label: Best picks
best.rule: the selections with the strongest evidence of winning across every section, one per player, at most two per game

instructions: Study every angle before choosing: defensive matchups, weather, injuries, confirmed starters, man-to-man matchups, stats, tendencies and defensive weak points, and any other variable the evidence calls for.
Do not let the odds determine or influence a selection: choose on evidence, then show the DraftKings price and what it implies.
Only DraftKings' actual posted lines. No alternate lines. No over/under on passing touchdowns.
Every section needs at least one selection; fill a section only with selections the research supports, up to its maximum.
Best picks are the selections with the highest evidence of actually winning, three to six of them, one per player, at most two from the same game.

availability.label: Availability: official report, practice participation, beat-writer notes, confirmed starters

weather.label: Weather at kickoff: wind, gusts, rain, temperature, roof

matchup.label: Defensive matchup: pass and run defense by EPA and success rate, pressure vs protection, tight-end coverage, defensive weak points

cornerbacks.label: Man-to-man matchups: shadow cornerback, slot vs wide, who guards whom

usage_form.label: Usage and form, last four games: routes, targets, carries, snap share trend, air yards

tendencies.label: Tendencies: pass rate over expected, pace, red-zone usage, how the offense attacks this defense

game_script.label: Game script: spread, total, pace, expected plays, who leads

line_movement.label: Line movement: opener vs now, with or without news

situational.label: Situational: rest, travel, short week, coordinator changes, resting starters

stadium.label: Stadium and surface effects (altitude, turf, dome)

desk_config.note: The NFL research desk's spec. The scheduled desk runs follow this file exactly; the page renders the sections it lists. Edit here (or ask Claude) to change how the desk thinks; the page's Desk settings panel only filters what is shown on your own phone.
desk_config.odds_rule_note: ignore = evidence picks the selection, the DraftKings price is shown but never decides; band = only prices inside odds_band are eligible
desk_config.lines_note: selections are on DraftKings' actual posted line only; no alternate lines

schedule.label: Final pass on Sunday + Monday night

desk_config.schedule_note: When the scheduled desk runs fire in the owner's Claude chat (America/Toronto; day 0 = Sunday). Information for the app only: changing it here does not move the tasks.
